## 306332da48b4

**Reproduced defect A306-1 — the advertised exact `n_blobs` control is ignored.** On immutable generator SHA-256 `d2add67c7f920652de56c143dd5875017c1638b0bfc720642c6d40c20e7211be` (version 1.1.1), canonical rule hash `6c8e8d01eb23`, seed **17**, sample index **0**, difficulty **medium**, `n_blobs=3` returns **two** isolated color components. Changing only the override to `n_blobs=2` returns the identical grid. These are two calls on one unique input, not a population estimate. The input is 8 rows × 12 columns: color 6 at `(3,6),(4,6),(5,6)` and color 8 at `(2,7),(2,8),(2,9),(3,8)`, all coordinates zero-based. `generate` obtains the count with `rng.randint(2,3)` rather than reading the override. Both calls pass `self_check` with `[]`; the grid belongs to the documented generator domain (2–3 distinct-color blobs, sizes ≥3, interior and separate centers). It violates the requested count, rather than being an invalid-grid counterexample. The supported Racket `apply` call succeeds and returns two five-cell crosses, centered at `(4,6)` and `(2,8)`. There is no reference-label defect in this witness. Recommended repair: consume and validate the advertised exact count before selecting the palette, or stop advertising that control. The source also bypasses the declared palette controls; those were observed in code but were not separately measured here.

**Reproduced distribution restriction A306-2 — generated examples cannot teach component detection across repeated colors.** The exact Racket rule finds orthogonally connected **nonzero** components, uses each component's modal color, floors each inclusive bbox midpoint, and draws a clipped five-cell cross. The generator instead samples a distinct color once for each blob and uses `grow_blob`, which makes each blob connected and forbids orthogonal adjacency to previous content. Consequently one bbox per color is equivalent to the reference on its ordinary generated domain. The retained executable rival preserves first-occurrence color ordering so output overlap order does not create an artificial distinction. It matches the retained generated Racket label, yet matches only **1/5 canonical labeled pairs** (four train plus one test, inspected from the public authoring view). It disagrees with the first canonical training input, whose three diagonal color-4 cells are three separate components: the reference draws three crosses, while the rival draws one at the color-global bbox center. The supported canonical-witness Racket call reproduces the recorded canonical output and rejects the rival. The canonical witness passes the generator's weak validator with `[]` but is outside its ordinary documented generator domain, because it contains three singleton components of the same color. This is an established support gap, not a claim that the rival fits canonical examples or that a saved generated label is wrong. A curriculum consisting only of this generator's ordinary draws cannot distinguish the two rules, even with arbitrarily many such draws. Recommended repair: include repeated-color separated components and diagonal singleton arrangements, then retain lessons that distinguish component-based processing from color-global processing.

**Domain question:** the public written solution says every component has an odd-by-odd bbox, but this accepted ordinary generated grid contains a 2×3 bbox for color 8. The Racket authority explicitly floors its center to `(2,8)`. No rule change is proposed: decide whether the written odd-bbox restriction should be enforced in generation or revised to document the floored-center extension. The current task notes are a placeholder and declare no further semantic limits or lesson competitors. This audit does not certify lesson identifiability against other rivals, and no model benchmark was run.

Exact grids, overrides and acceptance results: `checks/audit/306332da48b4/probe.json`, `input.json`, and `verification.json`. Actual generated Racket output and bound hashes: `checks/audit/306332da48b4/racket.json` (rule-text SHA-256 `4c1a46cf92a3c9368ce3c4aa8e7dfbaccaf1ea46558b6b03794499c0c8fb2ecb`). Rival output, all five canonical-fit booleans and the canonical witness: `checks/audit/306332da48b4/shortcut.json`; canonical Racket execution: `canonical-racket.json`; public task view: `show.json`. Reproduce using `probe.py`, `shortcut.py` and `verify.py`, with the exact successful commands, outer working directory, effective runtime directory and retained evidence recorded in `checks/audit/306332da48b4/commands.json`. All audited task and shared source files were left unchanged.

## 306332da48b4

**Reproduced ignored exact control on unchanged source; no audit-target files
were edited.** Current generator SHA-256 is
`d2add67c7f920652de56c143dd5875017c1638b0bfc720642c6d40c20e7211be`.
The advertised `n_blobs` axis is not read: the implementation chooses the count
with `rng.randint(2, 3)`.

At seed `17`, sample index `0`, difficulty `medium`, requesting `n_blobs=2` and
requesting `n_blobs=3` returns the **identical 8×12 grid**. Both calls pass
`self_check` with `[]`, and both contain exactly two components (color 6 with
three cells and color 8 with four cells). Thus the `n_blobs=3` request is
observably violated rather than rejected as incompatible.

The exact grid is retained in `checks/audit/306332da48b4/input.json`; supported
canonical Racket execution (rule hash `6c8e8d01eb23`) succeeds and draws the two
five-cell crosses, confirming this is an override-contract defect rather than a
label failure. Reproduction and structured records are in
`checks/audit/306332da48b4/probe.py`, `probe.json`, `probe.stdout.log`, and
`racket.json`.

The optional strict audit check found no task-local/frozen tests and failed for
missing `strict_canonical_like`, witnesses, and `lesson_identifiable`; see
`checks/audit/306332da48b4-combined/`. The source-matched prior audit also notes a
repeated-color curriculum support gap; I inspected that lead but did not rerun a
population census here. Recommended repair remains: consume and strictly
validate `n_blobs` (and other advertised controls) or remove them from `AXES`,
then add an executable semantic contract and repeated-color component cases.
